status: OSW editorial classification of NASA-identified records; NASA support level and motion form are independent facets
rule: Assign one primary form to every identified NASA record. A class or process remains a class or process even when a video shows many individual examples. These labels do not establish a dated footprint or eddy identity.
class_relation_rule: The subtype links below are OSW editorial taxonomic relationships among NASA-described classes across releases. They are not NASA assertions that one named individual was seen in two movies, and they do not transfer a parent's geography to a subtype.

forms.boundary_current: A named current along the western margin of an ocean basin in NASA's tour.
forms.throughflow: A named interbasin flow through a strait or island passage.
forms.overflow: Saline water flowing from a marginal sea into an adjacent basin, as NASA describes it.
forms.current_class: A dynamical group of currents, rather than one bounded current.
forms.meander: A bend or looping change in a current path; NASA does not identify an individual meander here.
forms.current_turn: A described change in the direction of a current, without an independently named flow in NASA's wording.
forms.eddy_class: An identified group or region of eddies without individual NASA names or tracks.
forms.retroflection: A current turn back toward its source basin, described as a ring-shedding region.
forms.ring_class: A group of detached rings; no individual ring identity is implied.
forms.deep_counterflow: A described flow below and opposite the surface current, without a distinct proper name from NASA.
forms.circulation_system: A connected large-scale circulation concept, not one mapped streamline.
forms.sinking_region: A described regional descent of water with no NASA-delineated footprint.
forms.vertical_process: A general vertical movement process, not one geographic individual.
